clue.text: Look here, there's more to come

definitions.meaning: an instruction to keep your eyes on a particular spot
a promise that further news or developments will follow

explanation.surface: A presenter teases viewers that the show has another segment coming up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal request to keep looking at one spot and the idiom promising future developments.

clue.text: Brace favourites to get up and dance

parts.note: a brace is a pair, i.e. two

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: favourites are pets, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A couple of favoured guests are urged to rise and take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns PETS into STEP, read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick ballroom routine in duple time is named this, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Brave guy that presents that girl with ring

parts.note: a pronoun for a female person, her
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A courageous man proposes, presenting a woman with a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A courageous man admired for bravery is a champion or heroic figure, a synonym.

clue.text: Hurried pronouncedly on a path, making retreat

indicators.note: pronouncedly says the previous word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: hied is an old verb meaning hurried
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Someone rushes along a trail to escape to a quiet bolt-hole.
explanation.walkthrough: HIED, an archaic word for hurried, is said like HIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded place to escape to is a retreat, a synonym for a hiding place.

clue.text: Supports parades

definitions.meaning: structural braces or props in a framework
walks with a swagger, showing off

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for structural props and a verb for walking proudly and showily.

clue.text: Gather below Dover perhaps is castle entrance

indicators.note: in a down entry, being below means this piece is written after the previous one

parts.note: Dover is an example of a port, the English Channel harbour town
to cull is to gather or pick out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gathering near Dover, someone finds the gateway to a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy grating lowered to block a castle gateway guards the entrance.

clue.text: Flattered little woman the French rogue's cuddling

indicators.note: cuddling means holding something close inside the arms, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
Jo is one of the March sisters in the novel Little Women
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A charming scoundrel sweet-talks a petite woman while hugging her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' suggests any small woman, but it points to Jo March of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone with flattery and wheedling is to sweet-talk them, a synonym.

clue.text: List of accusations — rush these to be reviewed

parts.note: to charge is to rush forward

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters of the word these are looked over again and rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman hurries to have a set of charges looked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reviewed' rearranges THESE into SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A police record listing the offences a suspect is charged with is this document.

clue.text: Wow, other ranks will eat free in hall

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like wow
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, non-officers
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Amazed, the soldiers find they can dine for nothing in the mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation; 'will eat' has the two outer pieces swallow the verb meaning free.
explanation.definitionFit: A long passage inside a building is a hallway, so hall is a synonym.

clue.text: Prince shows bottle going round a hospital

indicators.note: going round means the word jar is turned to face the other way

parts.note: a jar is a container like a bottle
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A royal shows off a bottle being taken round a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the container backwards; the result is also the name for British rule in India.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian king or princely ruler bore this title, so a prince is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Start a conversation? It's what travellers do in the Arctic

definitions.meaning: to ease the awkwardness when strangers first meet and get talking

definitions.text: It's what travellers do in the Arctic
definitions.meaning: literally, explorers or ships crossing polar seas must smash through frozen water

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for easing social awkwardness is also the literal act of smashing frozen sea to pass.

clue.text: Scribe topped and tailed ceremony

indicators.note: topping and tailing removes the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: A scribe trimmed at both ends at a formal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' strips W and R from WRITER.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn ritual act, especially religious, is a ceremony, a synonym.

clue.text: Painstaking detail

definitions.meaning: fussy and very careful about details
an individual item or point, as in 'in every respect'

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning fastidious and a noun meaning a single item of information.

clue.text: See company proposal for moving capacity

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A firm puts forward a motion about moving its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The power or ability to move from place to place is this, a synonym.

clue.text: Respect dad backing professional versus a learner

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word pa runs backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pro is short for professional
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A father supports a sports pro against a novice and earns their respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Favourable regard or esteem for someone is respect, a near synonym.

clue.text: Promise parking can be found by lake shore?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on signs
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
the shore is the edge of the water

explanation.surface: A promise that parking is available beside a lakeside beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn undertaking or vow is a promise, a synonym.

clue.text: Not a chain in southern Europe but one in northern England

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is left out of the mountain range

parts.note: the Apennines are the mountain chain running down Italy

explanation.surface: Pointing out which mountain range is Italian and which is English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' drops the first A from APENNINES. The Pennines are the hill range running down northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The range forming England's backbone is a mountain chain in the north of the country.

clue.text: Home brewer

parts.note: suggests an amateur beer maker but means the household pot that brews tea

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen vessel in which leaves are steeped is the thing that brews at home.

clue.text: Sprain I developed, painkiller needed

indicators.note: developed means the letters of the words grow into a new shape

explanation.surface: After a sprained ankle develops, someone needs a pill for the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A common analgesic tablet is an example of a painkiller.

clue.text: Diabolical meal causing misfortune inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal
evil can mean harm or misfortune

explanation.surface: A dreadful dinner that brings bad luck in its wake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal' looks like the definition but is the container; 'inside' places the misfortune within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish or wicked like the Devil is diabolical, a synonym.

clue.text: I will put on the item about Guernsey etc criminal

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting on top means this piece comes first

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: CI stands for Channel Islands, of which Guernsey is one
it can mean the thing or item in question

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stick a label on goods about the Channel Islands, which is criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CI into IC. The Channel Islands, including Guernsey and Jersey, lie off northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by law is unlawful, so criminal is a synonym.

clue.text: Pain that's left after surgery

definitions.meaning: a sharp pain in the side, as after running
a loop of suture thread remaining in a wound after an operation

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden side pain and a suture closing a surgical wound.

clue.text: Applying first of gears to follow former pilot manoeuvring in

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the others

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: manoeuvring suggests the letters of the word are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Using a gear change, an ex-pilot manoeuvres his way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges PILOT into PLOIT; 'first of gears' gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Making use of something to advantage is applying or utilising it, a synonym.

clue.text: Decomposed fuel outlet

indicators.note: decomposed means broken down, so the letters are put together again differently

explanation.surface: Rotting fuel finds a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct carrying smoke away is an outlet for fumes.

clue.text: Found written inside maze, Talmudic Greek character

indicators.note: the letters are found written within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Greek letter turns up inscribed in a puzzling Talmudic text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found written inside' points to the letters spanning maze and Talmudic.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth letter of the Greek alphabet is an example of a Greek character.

clue.text: Fancy that American soldier? Snappy little tyke!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GI is the term for a US soldier

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised by a GI who is a bad-tempered little scamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Welsh herding dog is known for nipping, so this snappy little breed is the dog.

clue.text: Number study city's outskirts — it's a trend

parts.note: ten is a number
a den is a private study

indicators.note: the outskirts are the outer edges, so only the first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A number of studies of urban fringes reveal a trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts' takes the outer letters C and Y of city; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclination or drift in a particular direction is a trend, a synonym.

clue.text: Shut it — nuisance when liquid is lukewarm

indicators.note: liquid means flowing and fluid, so the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tells an annoying person to be quiet when a drink is only tepid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking keenness or eagerness is lukewarm in its figurative sense.
